recommendations.finding: Newly quoted CIs/P values lack supporting Methods. Results currently refer readers to a presentation, which is not self-contained.
recommendations.ready_to_insert: For the overall confirmed and substantive counts, differences were defined as later minus earlier in candidates per paper. We used 95% percentile bootstrap intervals from 20,000 resamples of whole papers within each publication period (seed 20261022). Exact two-sided permutation tests compared the absolute mean differences across all allocations of 19 of the 44 papers to the earlier group, including ties. These exploratory P values were unadjusted; no category-level hypothesis tests were conducted.
recommendations.evidence: slides/calculate_results.R; slides/data/period_comparisons.csv. Independent Python integer dynamic program reproduced P = 0.682894948647625 and 1.0.

recommendations.finding: Opaque relationship codes and missing-data checks leave avoidable ambiguity about the corpus.
recommendations.ready_to_insert: The original relationship codes restricted eligibility to comparisons between report documents (S_C) or within one report document (S_W); report documents included non-plan results supplements. All 139 eligible Notes were nonempty and had unique year/paper/candidate keys, so no case required a title-only assignment. Validation confirmed that every retained evidence excerpt was an exact substring of its source Note and that the final human labels remained unchanged.

recommendations.finding: Alphabetic words and adjacent pairs alone do not fully specify the lexical representation; the nested substantive lexical corpus is not stated.
recommendations.ready_to_insert: Lexical summaries were produced for the 139 confirmed Notes and separately for the nested 37 substantive Notes. Numbers were preserved in the analytical text but excluded from word frequencies. Bigrams required adjacent words within segments bounded by punctuation or numbers; removing stopwords did not join the remaining words across a gap. Singular and plural forms remained separate. These choices were confined to the lexical representation and did not alter the verbatim text used for coding.

recommendations.finding: Taxonomy is operational and category frequency is not severity. The concise table correctly limits counts to primary categories, but an explicit category/status distinction and within-category fractions improve interpretation.
recommendations.ready_to_insert: The taxonomy was designed for this corpus. Each primary category represented the central retained mechanism; overlapping secondary categories and tags preserved additional concerns without contributing further counts. Local transcription or formatting tags did not determine substantive status. In this sample, 4 of 39 count/denominator candidates (10.3%) were substantive, compared with 8 of 14 effect-estimate candidates (57.1%) and 6 of 12 attribution candidates (50.0%). These fractions describe the inherited human labels within each category; they do not establish that a mechanism is inherently minor or substantive.
recommendations.evidence: taxonomy_final.json primary_selection_rules and secondary_categories; category_summary.csv; independent counts.

recommendations.finding: The report discusses composition but Table 2 reports counts and paper means rather than shares. A short share paragraph recovers the main compositional pattern without a third table.
recommendations.ready_to_insert: Among all confirmed candidates, count/denominator problems accounted for 23.2% in the earlier period and 31.3% in the later period, while analysis-definition problems accounted for 5.4% and 20.5%. Interval problems accounted for 25.0% and 12.0%, and attribution problems for 12.5% and 6.0%. These shares used 56 and 83 as their denominators; corresponding substantive shares used the nested totals of 16 and 21.
recommendations.evidence: category_period_summary.csv; independently verified all 28 count cells. Retain the existing zero-inclusive mean table.

recommendations.finding: Candidate dependence, sampling/detection limits and conditional bootstrap uncertainty are partly compressed away. Selected sample and no causal pandemic inference are already present, but they do not fully explain the uncertainty estimates.
recommendations.ready_to_insert: Candidates clustered within papers, which was why the paper was the resampling and permutation unit. The intervals describe uncertainty conditional on the available papers, detected candidates and final review decisions; they do not account for missed findings or adjudication uncertainty. The selected corpus therefore cannot estimate error prevalence among all trials, establish changes in research quality, or identify an effect of the publication period or pandemic. Similar observed substantive means also do not establish equivalence between periods.
recommendations.evidence: Archived full narrative sections 7 and 10; slides/calculate_results.R; scope of the availability sample. The last sentence is a statistical interpretation safeguard, not a new analysis.
